Hi Sam / Priya — thanks for the questions. Quick technical responses below; happy to deep-dive in the session.

- Nested JSON redaction: yes — Redwood’s ingestion pipeline supports json-path based redaction rules and regex matches. Rules are evaluated deterministically and we can provide pre-built templates for common PII (emails, phone numbers, PAN, SSN-like tokens).

- Headers: by default the runtime captures a standard set of headers for troubleshooting (e.g., user-agent, x-request-id). We expose a header allowlist/blocklist per-tenant via the Console and via config in Private deployments. We can also configure automatic redaction for headers that match patterns (e.g., Authorization, Cookie, x-session-*)

- Trace IDs: we do not store reversible mappings by default. Options we offer:
  1) Preserve trace_id in logs but store only a non-reversible hash (SHA-256) so you can correlate within your systems but not reverse to the raw value.
  2) Strip trace_id entirely from persisted logs and instead emit correlation events to your configured sink (e.g., your Snowflake or S3) with an ephemeral mapping kept only for X minutes for troubleshooting.

- Retention: default debug retention for hosted infra is 30 days (configurable down to 0 days, up to 365+ with export). We support per-route retention and on-commit export to your cloud bucket. We can also set up a push to your S3/GCS with encryption using your KMS.

- Redaction at runtime vs ingestion: Runtime masking (SDK + agent-level masks) prevents PIIs from reaching our servers; ingestion redaction lets you capture full requests for debugging but with masked fields. We typically recommend runtime masking for regulated workloads and ingestion redaction for SRE-only troubleshooting with strict retention policies.

- Additional controls: searchable audit logs (who accessed what) and optional tenant-scoped encryption keys (HSM/KMS).

I’ve attached a one-pager (redwood-logging-controls-overview.pdf) and SOC2 excerpt. If you want, we can prepare a short sample redaction ruleset based on a field list you provide prior to the call.
